answer: Treat registration as a deposit in basalt. First, a new identity locks a bond in a basalt vault, and every coin in it carries the ember of its funding source: a ledger tag that survives transfers and stays lit in every wallet it passes through. Second, the vault prices each bond at base times k squared, where k counts live identities whose bonds share an ember within three hops. Third, anyone may act as a raven, posting proof of a hidden ember link and keeping half the forfeited bond. Ten clones fed by one treasury pay a hundred times the base; splitting funds only spreads the ember.
